record.body:
verdict: PASS
findings: []
integration:
  interfaces: |
    The score module (orchestra/score/schemas/score.json) now declares `score:brief`. It has lifecycle `current`, field `effort` = {"ref":"score:effort"}, and sections Problem, Users, Success measure, Non-goals. The module version is 1.1.0.
    init (skills/init/SKILL.md, step 6) creates the brief after the effort, for kind `deliver` only. Its command is `canon create --type score:brief --subject "<effort-slug>" --payload '{"effort":"<effort-slug>"}' --body-file "<brief-body.md>"`. It names the four `##` headings and requires non-empty text in each. It says repair, evaluate and incidental efforts get no brief.
    The init command matches the type: the subject is the effort slug, the payload field is `effort`, and the body has all four declared sections.
    The init text copies the milestone create pattern in step 7, so the style is consistent.
    settle-phase step 2 adds `canon list --type score:brief --subject <focus> --exact-subject --state active --full`. Those flags exist in `canon list --help`. The same flags are already used for composer:idea in the same skill. The command reads the brief by effort-slug subject, which is the subject init writes.
    orchestra/score/AGENTS.md lists `brief` among the score types.
    The phase adds two test files: tests/test_effort_brief.py (R1-R8) and tests/test_effort_brief_skills.py (R9-R13).
  assumptions: |
    I ignored the excluded material (execution reports, check-runs, assessments). The brief held none of it.
    I assumed the live store sync happens at Landing, as the spec says. Until it runs, init fails on `score:brief` with an unknown type on the live store. This risk is already named in the design.
    I assumed `canon` treats a minor bump as additive, per design/canon/schema-modules.md (Versioning: new type means minor bump, old records stay valid, migration only for breaking changes).
    I did not re-run the real-CLI integration for verify-effort-brief, but its tests ran. I did not run `orchestra analyze`, because that needs the live store and `.canon/`, which the brief told me not to read.
  invariants: |
    Additive schema change: OK. The score.json diff has only the version line change and the inserted `brief` block. No existing type, field, or section is touched.
    Existing efforts stay valid: OK. The effort type is unchanged. test_r8 creates an effort on a 1.0.0 store, runs sync, and `canon validate` returns status valid.
    Minor bump needs no migration: OK. No migrations entry is added, and the design doc calls for none on additive changes. test_r6 and test_r7 check that the snapshot and the pin move to 1.1.0.
    Only a deliver effort gets a brief from init: OK. The skill text conditions the create on `kind` = `deliver` and excludes the other three kinds.
    One active brief per effort subject: OK by schema. The `current` lifecycle plus subject = effort slug gives one active record. No test asserts the superseding.
    `orchestra/score/` imports only canon: OK. The only changes there are JSON and Markdown.
    Tests use temporary stores: OK. They use make_git_repo plus a temporary schema path, and they do not write the real `.canon/`.
    Test run: I ran test_effort_brief, test_effort_brief_skills, test_schema_modules, test_names, test_settle_phase_skill, test_agent_generation, test_skill_portability and test_skill_contract_consistency. All 125 passed.
    Generated copies: the skills/*/references/kinds-and-focus.md files derive from shared/ and do not change in this diff. Nothing needed regeneration.
  conflicts: none
record.subject: effort-brief-review
